package_info.why_malicious: The affected versions of Drupal Core contain a critical reflected DOM-based XSS vulnerability (CVE-2020-13663) that allows authenticated users with content creation permissions to inject and execute arbitrary JavaScript in the context of other users. This enables attackers to hijack accounts, steal sessions, or inject persistent malicious content, posing a severe risk to site integrity and user security.

execution_context.trigger: Form submission with an expired or invalid CSRF token (rejected form submission).
execution_context.file_location: node/add/[type] and node/[node-id]/edit endpoints (web form handler, PHP/HTML/JS context).
required_permissions: Ability to use Full HTML mode

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon form submission with an expired or invalid CSRF token, the application reflects the unsaved form content—including injected HTML and JavaScript—back into the error page, where it is rendered inside a CKEditor instance. The injected <script> tag executes in the browser context, resulting in arbitrary JavaScript execution within the user's session.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The snippet demonstrates direct reflection and execution of user-supplied HTML and JavaScript in the browser, a hallmark of DOM-based XSS. The use of <iframe> and <script> tags is a known evasion technique to bypass WYSIWYG editor filtering, allowing the payload to execute despite intended sanitization.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Web applications should sanitize and encode user input, especially in error or rejected form states, to prevent execution of arbitrary code. Instead, the application reflects unsanitized HTML/JS, violating the principle of output encoding and safe error handling.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use may involve rendering user-supplied rich text or HTML in a WYSIWYG editor, but never unsanitized or executable script content. Proper implementations always filter or encode potentially dangerous tags.
key_indicators: Reflection of user-supplied HTML/JS in form error pages
Execution of <script> tags in the browser context via CKEditor
Bypassing CKEditor XSS filtering using <iframe> encapsulation
Triggering on form rejection due to expired or invalid CSRF token
Presence of Full HTML mode in content creation

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts a POST request to node/add/[type] or node/[node-id]/edit with a malicious payload in the body field, using Full HTML mode.
attack_chain.leads_to: Form submission is rejected due to missing or invalid CSRF token, but the malicious payload is reflected in the error page.

attack_chain.action: The error page displays the unsaved form content in a CKEditor instance, rendering the injected HTML and JavaScript.
attack_chain.leads_to: CKEditor processes the content, and the injected <script> tag is executed in the browser context.

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript executes in the victim's browser, enabling account hijacking, session theft, or further malicious actions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains control over the victim's session or injects additional malicious content.

behavioral_signatures: Reflection of user-supplied HTML or JavaScript in form error pages
Execution of <script> tags within CKEditor or similar WYSIWYG editors on error pages
Presence of <iframe> and <script> tags in form body fields during rejected submissions
Form rejection events followed by rendering of unsanitized user input
file_indicators: node/add/* and node/*/edit endpoints processing POST data containing unsanitized HTML/JS
Form error pages that display raw HTML/JS from user input in the CKEditor instance
network_indicators: Unusual POST requests to node/add/* or node/*/edit endpoints with suspicious HTML/JS payloads in form fields
Subsequent HTTP requests or actions initiated by injected JavaScript, such as session hijacking or credential exfiltration
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor POST requests to content creation or edit endpoints for <script> or <iframe> tags in form fields, especially when followed by a form rejection error. Inspect rendered error pages for unsanitized HTML/JS reflection in CKEditor. Deploy web application firewalls (WAF) to block script/iframe injection in form fields, and audit CKEditor configurations to ensure proper XSS filtering is enforced. Regularly review error page rendering logic to confirm user input is always sanitized.
